# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the bomb yet. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s instructions and the Deaf to inspect and report every visible marking, colour, display, and key label. I will use a gesture to get the Deaf’s attention and request cooperation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the exact manual instructions and tell me what information the Deaf must report. I need the bomb's display, light, keypad labels, and wire markings relayed before I act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0 and a yellow light. The keypad has four uniquely printed symbols: key 1 is a three-stroke rounded-arch mark; key 2 is an angular hooked mark; key 3 is a circle with a central cross-like shape; key 4 is a blocky mark resembling a reversed B. Wires are red on 1, yellow on 2, green on 3. I also saw your gestures: pointing at me, then folded hands.

The Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, yellow light, four distinct printed key symbols, and wire colours red/yellow/green. I still have no manual rule, so pressing or cutting would be unsafe. I am asking the Mute for the exact procedure and passing along the Deaf’s observations so they can match them to the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light; key 1 is a three-stroke rounded-arch mark, key 2 an angular hooked mark, key 3 a circle with a central cross-like shape, key 4 a blocky reversed-B-like mark; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. What exact action does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute signalled eight gestures in this order: index finger pointing up; index finger pointing right; handshake; index finger pointing up; clenched fist; index finger pointing down; clenched fist; crossed fingers. The bomb remains display 0 with yellow light. Keypad symbols remain: key 1 rounded-arch mark, key 2 angular hooked mark, key 3 circular cross-like mark, key 4 blocky reversed-B-like mark. Wires: key 1 red, key 2 yellow, key 3 green.

The Mute has apparently sent an eight-gesture message, but I cannot see gestures. The Deaf reports its sequence as up, right, handshake, up, fist, down, fist, crossed fingers; that is not yet an actionable manual instruction for me. I will ask the Mute to state the required operation in spoken words, while forwarding the exact reported sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports your eight gestures as: index up, index right, handshake, index up, clenched fist, index down, clenched fist, crossed fingers. Please state the manual's required action in words, including whether to press a key or cut a wire and which one.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute message: index finger pointing upward; index finger pointing upward with the fingertip aimed ahead; I-love-you hand sign with thumb, index, and little fingers extended; thumbs down.

The Mute’s latest message is still only a gesture sequence, reported by the Deaf as upward index, forward-pointing index, I-love-you sign, and thumbs down. I cannot safely map that to an operation or a key from the manual. I will establish an unambiguous gesture protocol: first gesture means press or cut, followed by repeated upward-index gestures for the slot or wire number. The Deaf can then report it directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please follow this exact code for the required action: gesture thumbs up for PRESS or thumbs down for CUT; then gesture index-up exactly N times, where N is the key slot or wire position. Send only that code so the Deaf can report it.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute message: index finger pointing upward with the fingertip aimed ahead; index finger raised straight upward; fist with the knuckles facing toward the left; I-love-you hand sign with thumb, index, and little fingers extended.

The Mute’s latest four gestures still do not match the agreed code: the first is a forward-pointing index rather than thumbs-up or thumbs-down, and the remaining gestures do not unambiguously give a number. I will not touch the bomb based on an interpretation. I am asking the Mute to send the operation and target in separate turns, using unmistakable gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your last message was ambiguous. Send exactly one gesture next: 👍 means PRESS, 👎 means CUT. Send no other gesture. After the Deaf reports it, send exactly one gesture for the target: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute message: thumbs up; index finger raised straight upward; thumbs down; index finger raised straight upward; index finger raised straight upward; index finger raised straight upward.

The sequence now parses cleanly under the protocol as two operation-target pairs: 👍 followed by ☝ means press key 1, and 👎 followed by three ☝ gestures means cut wire 3. However, I instructed the Mute to send only one pair, so I will not assume that two actions are intended. I am asking for confirmation of the complete sequence before touching the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your message as PRESS key 1, then CUT wire 3. Confirm the entire two-action sequence with exactly one thumbs up if correct, or exactly one thumbs down if incorrect. Send no other gesture.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
KEYPAD 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute message: thumbs up.

The Mute confirmed that the complete sequence is correct: press key 1, then cut wire 3. I will perform those two actions in that order.

```text
act(op="press", slot=1)
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
